condition: Corner lot, secondary boundary setback, dwellings and dual occupancies (general table control)
_dev_type_evidence: The table's own heading on page 9: 'Table 3.1.2-a: Minimum boundary setbacks for dwellings and dual occupancies'.
review_note: NEW and clean. Table 3.1.2-a's own heading on the page is 'Minimum boundary setbacks for dwellings and dual occupancies', and the row reads 'Secondary boundary 3m (on corner lots)'. LGA-wide, boundary-relative, ground level, mandatory table. Corroborated by our own data: hornsby already serves front, rear and side setbacks extracted from the same table (section_ref 's3.1.2-table-a'), so this completes that set with the one boundary that was missing. dev_type dwelling_house; the table also governs dual occupancies, which the next row states in its own terms.

condition: Corner lot, detached dual occupancy - the dwelling fronting the primary road must be setback from the secondary road boundary
source_text:
The dwelling fronting the main Primary Road
should have a minimum setback with the
secondary road of 3m (see Figure 3.1-g).
_dev_type_evidence: Page 9 prescriptive measure (h): 'An attached dual occupancy on a corner lot should have both dwellings address the primary road frontage'. The clause's subject is dual occupancy.
review_note: NEW. Prescriptive measure (h) on the same page reads 'An attached dual occupancy on a corner lot should have both dwellings address the primary road frontage', so the clause's subject is dual occupancy, and (i) gives it 3m to the secondary road. Same value as the dwelling-house row above, from a different clause about a different dev_type -- so not a duplicate: a consumer querying dual_occupancy would otherwise get nothing.

condition: ONLY WHERE a secondary frontage adjoins an EXISTING LANEWAY with no verge: all buildings and structures should be set back a minimum of 6 metres from that boundary. This is not hornsby's general secondary street setback for residential flat buildings.
source_text:
Where a secondary frontage adjoins an existing
laneway (with no verge), all buildings and
structures should be setback a minimum of 6
metres from the boundary.
_dev_type_evidence: Our own extracted provisions give the part title: '3.4 Residential Flat Buildings (5 Storeys)' (ref Hornsby_DCP_2024__hornsby_dcp_2024_part3_residential__3_4). Section 3.4.5 is its setbacks sub-section.
review_note: NEW, and the qualifier is the control. dev_type comes from our own extracted provisions, which give the part title as '3.4 Residential Flat Buildings (5 Storeys)'; 3.4.5 is its setbacks sub-section. The 6m applies only 'Where a secondary frontage adjoins an existing laneway (with no verge)'. That is a site condition, not a geography, so unlike the Pound Road rows below it is genuinely LGA-wide -- but served without its test it would read as hornsby's general apartment secondary setback, which it is not. Qualifier moved to the front of the condition.
